groups.title: PHP Core Concepts
groups.question: A login check in your PHP code lets a user in when it should not, because '0' compared equal to false, and a new class clashes with one from a package. Explain how PHP's types and namespaces work.

followUps.Type System and Type Juggling: Why can '0' == false be true, and how do you avoid surprises like this?
followUps.Namespaces and Autoloading: How do namespaces and PSR-4 autoloading find your classes?

evidence.text: Loose comparison with == converts values to a common type before comparing.
Strict comparison with === also checks the type, so different types are never equal.
Type declarations and strict types make PHP reject wrong types instead of converting them.

notEnough: Only saying to use triple equals.

misconceptions.text: Says == and === behave the same for strings and booleans.

evidence.text: Namespaces keep classes with the same name in different packages apart.
PSR-4 maps a namespace to a folder, so a class's namespace matches its file path.
Composer's autoloader loads classes on demand from those rules.

groups.title: Object-Oriented PHP
groups.question: You are writing payment gateways that must be swappable and several models that share the same 'sluggable' behaviour. Explain how interfaces, abstract classes and traits help.

followUps.Interfaces and Abstract Classes: When would you use an interface and when an abstract class?
followUps.Traits and Code Reuse: How do traits share behaviour, and what happens when two traits define the same method?

evidence.text: An interface defines methods a class promises to implement, with no shared code.
An abstract class can share code and leave some methods for subclasses to fill in.
Code that depends on an interface can work with any implementation, which Laravel's container relies on.
Traits add methods to classes regardless of their inheritance.
Laravel uses traits like SoftDeletes and Notifiable.
Conflicting method names must be resolved explicitly with insteadof or aliases.

groups.title: Composer Dependency Management
groups.question: A teammate's install pulled a different version of a library and broke production. Explain how Composer manages versions.

followUps.Semantic Versioning and Version Constrai: What do the ^ and ~ constraints allow?

evidence.text: composer.lock records the exact version of every installed package.
composer install uses it so every environment gets identical code.
Only composer update changes the versions, and that should be deliberate.

notEnough: Only saying the lock file locks versions.

evidence.text: Semantic versions are major.minor.patch, where a major bump may break things.
^2.0 allows any 2.x version but not 3.0.
~2.1 allows 2.1 and later 2.x versions, but not 3.0, while ~2.1.0 allows only 2.1.x patches.

notEnough: Only saying they set version ranges.

groups.title: PHP Built-in Functions
groups.question: Your import script runs out of memory on a large CSV and user names with accents get cut in the middle. Explain how you would process the data and handle text safely.

followUps.Array Functions and Performance: When would you use a generator instead of array_map on a large dataset?
followUps.String Handling and Multibyte Safety: Why do strlen and substr break on accented text, and what should you use?

evidence.text: Array functions like array_map and array_filter work on whole arrays in memory.
Generators with yield produce one value at a time.
Generators keep memory low for large files or result sets.
strlen and substr count bytes, not characters.
In UTF-8 one character can be several bytes, so cutting by bytes can split characters.
Multibyte functions like mb_strlen and mb_substr work on characters.

notEnough: Only saying to use mb functions.
